Faster deploys for apps that pass an IAM role to their functions, and Router timeout docs that match what CloudFront does. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

### Fixes

- **A function no longer reads the IAM role you pass to it on every deploy.** With `role` set, SST looked the role up once per function on every `sst dev` and `sst deploy`, even when nothing had changed, so an app that shares one role across many functions paid for it many times. On a test app with 150 functions sharing one role, that was 150 reads per run, and it is now 0; a deploy with nothing to change went from 21–26 seconds to 13–18 seconds. The role is read when you access `nodes.role`, and then a role that doesn't exist fails the deploy. Because of that, a role that was deleted no longer fails a deploy of an existing function: the function fails when it runs, with "The role defined for the function cannot be assumed by Lambda". The `role` docs now say so. The first deploy after you update changes none of your resources; it only drops the role reads from SST's state. ([#116](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/116), [anomalyco/sst#6942](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6942))

### Docs

- **The `readTimeout` and `keepAliveTimeout` options of a URL route on a `Router` (`router.route()`) now say what CloudFront does.** `readTimeout` counts for each connection attempt, so a request to a destination that never answers can take `readTimeout` times `connectionAttempts` (3 by default) to fail. `keepAliveTimeout` is passed to CloudFront but ignored: the connection is kept for the keep-alive timeout of the distribution's origin, 5 seconds by default. ([#112](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/112), [anomalyco/sst#6987](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6987), [anomalyco/sst#6900](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6900))

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.21.2
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.21.2"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
